Results: Of 1327 records (806 after deduplication), 91 full texts were assessed and 53 sources included (31 empirical; 22 secondary/prescriptive). Primary-care guidance was common, but empirical evidence from primary care was limited. Diagnostic delay of months to years was reported, and in one survey more than half of women consulted three or more clinicians before diagnosis. In one physician survey, supported by a smaller pilot survey, primary care physicians initiated hormone therapy less often than specialists, and gaps in long-term follow-up persisted. No formally evaluated shared-care model was identified. Conclusions: Primary care is central to recommended POI care, but implementation remains poorly studied. Research should quantify real-world primary care performance and test structured interdisciplinary pathways.

title: Obesity and Diabetes in Pregnancy and Maternal and Child Health: The Gerar Cohort Profile, Brazil.
abstract: Pre-pregnancy obesity and GDM increase maternal-fetal oxidative stress, but their consequences for women's health and child development are still unclear. This paper describes the methodological design, recruitment strategy, data collection methods, and baseline characteristics of the Gerar Cohort, a prospective longitudinal study designed to investigate the relationship between pre-pregnancy obesity and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) with oxidative stress biomarkers and their effects on maternal and child health outcomes through 12 months postpartum. Women were recruited early in their prenatal care in a city in Southern Brazil. Sociodemographic and clinical data, as well as blood samples, were collected each trimester. At childbirth, umbilical cord blood and placental tissue were collected. Children were followed up until 12 months of age, with blood collection at 4 and 12 months. The study was approved by the Research Ethics Committee. A total of 189 women were recruited in the first trimester; 136 were followed up until the third trimester; 23 pregnancy losses were recorded. Pre-gestational obesity was observed in 24.3% (95% CI 18.4-31.1), and 27% (95% CI 20.8-33.9) of women were diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus. Fifty-nine umbilical cord blood samples and 61 placental fragments were collected. In the children's follow-up, 71 children were taken for ophthalmological examination at 1 month of age; 60 attended the pediatric consultation at 4 months; 56 children attended the neurological evaluation at 6 months and 50 at 12 months. The Gerar Cohort successfully implemented its recruitment and biospecimen collection procedures within public healthcare services.

title: Trends in Prescription Medications Reflect the Current Substance Misuse Trends.
abstract: Background: In Israel, fentanyl and pregabalin prescription rates for pain management have increased over the years. However, Health Maintenance Organizations (HMOs) implemented restrictions on opioid prescribing in 2022, potentially reducing fentanyl availability while pregabalin prescribing remained unrestricted. We aimed to examine temporal trends in fentanyl and pregabalin misuse between 2021 and 2025 among individuals receiving methadone maintenance treatment (MMT) in Tel Aviv, in the context of changes in opioid prescribing policies, and to characterize fentanyl misuse groups. Methods: In this prospective descriptive study, between February 2021 and December 2025, patients (ranging from 291 to 311) were screened three to four times annually for fentanyl and pregabalin, in addition to other routine urine tests for substance use. Trends in positive urine screens for pregabalin and fentanyl were compared. Additionally, methadone doses and serum methadone levels were compared among patients who consistently tested positive for fentanyl (n = 15), tested negative for fentanyl (n = 202), or Stopped/Started fentanyl Use (n = 22) between 2023 and 2025. Results: Pregabalin positivity ranged between 11.2% and 15.9%, with no temporal trend. The fentanyl positivity rate increased from 9.8% in October 2021 to 15.1% in March 2023 and subsequently decreased to 7.5% in March 2025, paralleling the reported reduction in fentanyl availability following HMO restrictions. The methadone dose among patients testing positive for fentanyl was higher, whether they discontinued or continued fentanyl use, than among patients who consistently tested negative for fentanyl. Conclusions: Fentanyl positivity decreased following HMO restrictions and the associated reduction in fentanyl availability, whereas pregabalin positivity remained stable during the study period. Further research is needed to identify the distinct drivers of pregabalin misuse and evaluate appropriate prevention and prescribing strategies. Patients with fentanyl-positive urine screens may require higher methadone doses.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Remote Monitoring in Children with Mixed Dentition: Agreement with Clinical Assessment in a Prospective Pilot Study.
abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted remote monitoring is increasingly used in dentistry, but evidence in children who are not undergoing active orthodontic treatment remains limited. This prospective pilot study evaluated the agreement between an AI-based Observational Monitoring system and conventional clinical examination for selected oral health findings in children with mixed dentition. Methods: Twenty children (10 males and 10 females; mean age 10.5 years, range 9-12 years) were evaluated at baseline (T0), 6 months (T1), and 12 months (T2). Six clinical conditions-dental plaque, persistent dental calculus, minor food debris, mild gingivitis, satisfactory oral hygiene, and dental staining-were assessed by a clinical observer and by the DentalMonitoring Observational Monitoring system. None of the patients included in the study were undergoing orthodontic treatment. Observer and AI classifications were analyzed as paired data. For each condition and time point, observed agreement and Cohen's kappa were calculated from the paired 2 × 2 table, and systematic differences between methods were assessed with the exact McNemar test; changes in prevalence over time were assessed with Cochran's Q test. Results: Observed agreement ranged from 65% to 95% at T0, from 65% to 100% at T1, and from 85% to 100% at T2, with wide 95% confidence intervals (e.g., 65.0%, 95% CI 40.8-84.6%). Cohen's kappa ranged from -0.14 to 0.64 and was not computable when a condition was absent according to both methods. For low-prevalence findings, high observed agreement coincided with kappa values close to zero. For conditions with more balanced prevalence, chance-corrected agreement was only fair. During follow-up, the prevalence of dental plaque and food debris decreased, whereas that of satisfactory oral hygiene and dental staining increased. Conclusions: AI-assisted Observational Monitoring showed moderate-to-high observed agreement but variable chance-corrected agreement with direct clinical assessment in this small pediatric cohort. The system may represent a complementary tool for longitudinal dental follow-up, but professional supervision remains necessary and larger validation studies are required.

title: Effectiveness of Pain Neuroscience Education and Therapeutic Exercise in Adults with Musculoskeletal Pain: A Randomized Controlled Experimental Pilot Study.
abstract: Chronic musculoskeletal pain is a common public health problem with substantial functional and socioeconomic impact. Pain neuroscience education (PNE) has been proposed as a complementary strategy to therapeutic exercise; however, the available evidence shows considerable methodological variability and a limited number of studies evaluating its added effect in real-world clinical settings. This study evaluated the effect of incorporating a structured PNE programme into a therapeutic exercise protocol on pain intensity, kinesiophobia, and muscle strength in patients with musculoskeletal pain. A randomized controlled pilot trial was conducted in patients with chronic musculoskeletal pain. Participants were assigned to an experimental group (exercise + PNE) or a control group (exercise only). Participants were adults with chronic musculoskeletal pain of at least three months' duration, predominantly women, with pain located mainly in the lumbar region, followed by the neck, shoulder, and knee. The intervention lasted 8 weeks, and pain, kinesiophobia, and muscle strength were assessed before and after the intervention. Outcome comparisons were performed using intra- and intergroup non-parametric statistical analyses, with the significance level set at p < 0.05. No significant between-group differences were observed in pain intensity. The group receiving PNE showed greater improvements in kinesiophobia and fear-avoidance beliefs. Both groups significantly improved muscle strength, with no differences between them. Mean attendance at the PNE sessions was 88.3%; 31 of the 38 randomized participants (81.6%) were included in the final analysis, and no adverse events were observed. No statistically significant additional effect of PNE was detected on pain intensity or muscle strength in this pilot sample, although it was associated with greater reductions in kinesiophobia and fear-avoidance beliefs. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Effect of Trataka on Visual, Cognitive, and Psychophysiological Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: A complementary and alternative healthcare practice such as Trataka, a Yogic visual concentration technique (YVC) rooted in Ayurvedic tradition, links cognition, visual, and psychophysiological well-being. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the moderating factors, including variations in study design and intervention protocol, to understand the efficacy of YVC across multiple domains. Systematic searches of eight scientific databases obtained 34 studies from 280 records until December 2025. Based on task scores, meta-regression and statistical heterogeneity were assessed using a random-effects model to obtain standardized mean difference (SMD) and risk of bias (RoB). A pooled meta-analysis showed a significant YVC effect over control conditions across visual, cognitive, and psychophysiological domains (SMD of 0.92, 95% CI [0.44, 1.41]), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 74%) and a wide prediction interval (-0.22 to 2.07), which indicated that the true effect size could range from negligible to large, while extending to future studies. Meta-regression across the nine cognitive studies (K = 4 for each study design; k = 1 outlier) revealed no statistically significant duration-response relationship between session length and cognitive outcomes. RoB assessments indicated unclear to high risk among included studies. Our results indicate that regular YVC practice could be associated with potential benefits for ocular and cognitive wellbeing, and for stress reduction, aligned with Sustainable Development Goal 3. However, given substantial heterogeneity, methodological limitations, and RoB concerns among included studies, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Standardized protocols, larger controlled trials, and neuroimaging approaches are needed to more precisely characterize YVC-related effects.

title: Exercise Training in Patients with Established Cancer Cachexia: A Case Series.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Exercise is a supportive strategy for patients with cancer; however, evidence in individuals with established cancer cachexia remains limited. This study aimed to provide a preliminary description of feasibility and exploratory changes during a supervised exercise program in patients with cancer cachexia. Methods: Five women diagnosed with gastrointestinal or breast cancer and meeting the diagnostic criteria for cancer cachexia participated in a 12-week supervised exercise program, combining aerobic with resistance training, conducted twice weekly. Feasibility outcomes included completion, attendance, adherence, and adverse events. Muscle strength, flexibility, body composition, functional capacity, and patient-reported outcomes were assessed at baseline and post-intervention. Results: All participants completed the intervention and post-intervention assessments. Attendance ranged from 54% to 96%, with interruptions primarily related to treatment schedules and treatment-related side effects. No serious exercise-related adverse events occurred. Functional capacity improved in all participants (+ 33 to +73 m). Grip strength increased in all patients for the right hand (+0.5 to +5.5 kg) and in three patients for the left hand (+2.0 to +3.5 kg). Body composition responses were heterogeneous: fat-free mass increased in three patients (+1.3 to +2.8 kg), whereas two patients showed reductions. Fat mass decreased in three patients (-2.6 to -5.0 kg) and increased in two. Several domains of quality of life and symptom burden improved in most participants. Conclusions: In these five women with cancer cachexia, a supervised exercise program showed variable attendance and no serious exercise-related adverse events, whereas favorable changes for functional outcomes and heterogeneous response in body composition were observed.

title: Development and Psychometric Validation of a Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Questionnaire on Pulmonary Embolism and Its Modifiable Risk Factors (PE-KAP-RO): Protocol for a Cross-Sectional Study in Adults from Western Romania.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), whose most severe manifestation is pulmonary embolism (PE), is the third most common acute cardiovascular disorder, and many of its risk factors≠-obesity, physical inactivity, smoking, and unfavorable dietary patterns-are modifiable. No validated instrument is currently available to assess knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding PE among adults in Romania, and the burden of self-reported thromboembolic risk factors in community settings has not been described with standardized measures. This protocol describes the development and psychometric validation of the PE-KAP-RO questionnaire, an integrated assessment tool comprising three scored KAP scales, three embedded validated lifestyle instruments, and an exploratory, unweighted VTE risk-factor burden index. No participants had been enrolled and no data had been collected at the time of submission; all procedures are therefore described as planned. The study comprises two phases. Phase 1 (development) includes qualitative concept elicitation with members of the target population, guideline- and theory-anchored item generation, expert content validation quantified by the content validity index, and pilot testing with cognitive debriefing (n ≈ 30). Phase 2 is a cross-sectional field validation in at least 450 adults (≥18 years) from Western Romania-with recruitment continuing toward 600 where feasible-through combined in-person (quota-guided) and online sampling that includes healthcare professionals, with test-retest re-administration in a subsample of at least 60 participants after 14 ± 4 days. Physical activity, diet, and nicotine dependence will be measured with the IPAQ-SF, MEDAS, and FTND. Sample size is justified separately for each analysis (precision of proportions, correlation and regression power, events per variable, split-sample factor analysis, item response theory calibration, and reliability estimation). Measurement properties will be evaluated against pre-specified acceptance criteria: item difficulty 0.20-0.80 (a screening range interpreted together with discrimination) and corrected item-total correlations ≥ 0.30; internal consistency (KR-20/Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega) 0.70-0.95; test-retest ICC ≥ 0.70 and item-level weighted kappa ≥ 0.60; structural validity by split-sample exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis (CFI/TLI ≥ 0.90, RMSEA ≤ 0.08, SRMR ≤ 0.08); item response theory calibration with formal model comparison and differential item functioning screening; construct validity requiring confirmation of ≥75% of a priori hypotheses; floor/ceiling effects < 15%; and measurement invariance across sex, age group, and administration mode. The study will deliver a validated Romanian-language instrument, a structured characterization of PE-related knowledge, attitudes, and preventive practices, and the distribution of self-reported risk factors in the study sample. PE-KAP-RO is intended as a standardized assessment tool for PE-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices; the risk-factor burden index is descriptive and does not estimate VTE probability; any future predictive tool would require a separate cohort followed for incident VTE. Reporting follows the STROBE recommendations and COSMIN-based methodology; the protocol is presented prior to participant enrollment.

title: Psychological Distress, Daytime Sleepiness, Fatigue, and Health-Related Quality of Life in Young Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study with Implications for Rehabilitation.
abstract: This study examined associations between psychological distress, daytime sleepiness, mental and physical fatigue, and HRQoL in young adults and identified key predictors relevant for rehabilitation-oriented screening and intervention. In this cross-sectional analytical study, 371 university students (18-25 years) completed the Epworth Sleepiness Scale, Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21, Fatigue Assessment Scale, and 12-Item Short Form Health Survey. Descriptive statistics, one-way ANOVA, multivariate general linear models, multiple linear regression, and logistic regression were applied to evaluate associations with fatigue and SF-12 physical and mental health scores and categories. Most participants reported mild-moderate distress and fatigue, and about half of the participants had SF-12 scores below the sample median. Severe mental and physical fatigue were associated with substantially higher stress, anxiety, and depression than normal fatigue (all p < 0.001). Psychological variables explained 52% of the variance in mental fatigue and 30% in physical fatigue, with lower R2 for SF-12 physical (0.17) and mental health (0.29). Depression and stress were the strongest predictors of mental fatigue and low SF-12 mental health scores, whereas anxiety was more closely related to physical fatigue and physical health. Sleepiness showed weak, inconsistent associations after adjustment. Higher distress categories significantly increased the odds of HRQoL below the sample median. Psychological distress, particularly depression and stress, was strongly associated with fatigue and was also associated with poorer health-related quality of life, although the adjusted models indicated a more modest contribution to HRQoL. The findings support the value of considering psychological distress in rehabilitation-oriented screening while recognizing that HRQoL is influenced by multiple factors.

title: Differential Accuracy and Concordance of ChatGPT and DeepSeek for Image-Based Questions in Undergraduate Medical Education.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT (GPT) and DeepSeek (DS) are increasingly explored in medical education and practice. This study compared the accuracy and concordance of GPT and DS in answering multiple-choice Progress Test questions (2013-2024) across three input formats: text-only, image-only, and full-question (vignette + image). GPT achieved 72.9% overall accuracy versus 65.1% for DS, with moderate inter-model agreement (κ = 0.591). Critically, for both models, full-question accuracy did not exceed text-only accuracy, indicating that the addition of visual content provided no global incremental benefit. Conversely, accuracy dropped significantly in the image-only condition, confirming that isolated visual information was less informative than textual history. Category-specific analyses revealed relative strengths for GPT in skin and body pictures and for DS in microscopic and radiographic images, though these did not translate into an overall multimodal advantage. Questions answered correctly had lower difficulty indices, while discrimination indices did not differ between correct and incorrect responses, and performance was similar across cognitive levels. These findings demonstrate that, under the tested conditions, LLM performance was predominantly text-driven rather than visuospatially integrated. Accordingly, ChatGPT and DeepSeek function as proficient text-based clinical reasoners, but not as effective multimodal diagnostic systems in this educational assessment context. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40670-026-02839-9.

title: Comparative performance of nine large language models on professional Parkinson's disease tasks: a multidimensional benchmark study.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) requires both disease-specific knowledge and contextual clinical reasoning. However, most evaluations of medical large language models (LLMs) emphasize closed-ended questions and factual accuracy, providing limited insight into broader dimensions of performance on professional PD tasks. Nine contemporary LLMs were evaluated using a 200-item English-language professional PD benchmark spanning five clinical domains, four difficulty levels, and multiple question formats. Responses were assessed for expert-rated factual accuracy, clinical reasoning, Global Quality Scale (GQS), and Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL). The nine models generated 1,800 responses. Between-model separation was minimal for expert-rated factual accuracy (Kendall' s W = 0.031) but greater for FKGL (W = 0.235), Clinical Reasoning (W = 0.256), and GQS (W = 0.301). Between-model separation in expert-rated factual accuracy was small for closed-ended questions (W = 0.020, p = 0.001) but greater for open-ended questions (W = 0.121, p < 0.001). Expert-rated factual accuracy remained weakly discriminative across PD domains and difficulty levels, while GQS showed the greatest domain-specific separation in Safety & Ethics (W = 0.431). Flagship variants consistently showed higher Clinical Reasoning and GQS, but not uniformly higher factual accuracy. Contemporary LLMs showed limited between-model separation in expert-rated factual accuracy within this benchmark and scoring framework, whereas greater differentiation emerged in open-ended tasks, clinical reasoning, overall response quality, and readability. Multidimensional evaluation may therefore provide a more informative characterization of model performance and help inform task-specific model selection and oversight in medical applications.

title: A brief neuromotor-therapy-augmented pathway for pediatric functional movement disorders: a sequential historical cohort study.
abstract: Pediatric functional movement disorders (FMD) often improve, but access to specialized motor rehabilitation is heterogeneous. We compared two sequential, non-overlapping care periods within one clinical unit: usual care (UC) and a neuromotor-therapy-augmented pathway (NMT-A), which added brief hospital-based neuromotor therapy before community referral. This retrospective, non-randomized historical cohort included 17 UC patients (June 2021-January 2023) and 29 NMT-A patients (February 2023-June 2025). The primary outcome was continuous S-FMDRS at 6 months; S-FMDRS-defined motor symptom-free status (score = 0) was secondary. Both were reassessed at 12 months, together with community-treatment engagement. At 6 months, the adjusted NMT-A-minus-UC S-FMDRS difference was -1.66 points (95% CI, -4.04 to 0.72). Motor symptom-free status occurred in 55.2% versus 5.9% (risk difference, 49.3 percentage points; 95% CI, 21.8 to 66.4), and in 86.2% versus 52.9% at 12 months (risk difference, 33.3 percentage points; 95% CI, 6.5 to 56.8). The pathway-by-time interaction was not significant. Sustained community physical and/or occupational therapy was documented in 75.0% versus 17.6% (RR, 4.25; 95% CI, 1.74-12.46). The NMT-A pathway-period was associated with more frequent motor symptom-free status and greater continuity of community motor rehabilitation, although the adjusted mean S-FMDRS difference was not statistically significant. Because pathway and calendar period were inseparable, these findings should be interpreted as associations with the overall later care pathway rather than as an isolated effect of NMT.

title: Synaptic delays modulate population phase and amplitude responses in oscillatory excitatory-inhibitory networks.
abstract: Synaptic delays are fundamental determinants of neuronal communication and can profoundly influence the emergence and stability of cortical oscillations. Although their role in shaping network synchronization is well established, how synaptic delays regulate the collective response of neuronal populations to transient perturbations remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the effects of synaptic delays on the phase and amplitude responses of oscillatory activity in a conductance-based excitatory-inhibitory spiking network operating in the pyramidal-interneuron gamma (PING) regime. By systematically varying the synaptic delay and applying brief external perturbations to the excitatory population, inhibitory population, or the entire network, we computed network phase response curves (nPRCs) and network amplitude response curves (nARCs) to quantify changes in oscillation timing and population coherence. Increasing synaptic delay slowed network oscillations while enhancing population synchrony, demonstrating a trade-off between oscillation frequency and coherence. Excitatory perturbations produced relatively robust phase responses across delays but exhibited a pronounced delay-dependent reduction in amplitude enhancement. In contrast, inhibitory perturbations generated substantially stronger delay-dependent modulation of both phase resetting and amplitude suppression, whereas whole-network stimulation combined features of both excitatory and inhibitory responses. Taken together, these findings identify synaptic delay as a key parameter governing the balance between phase resetting and amplitude modulation and provide a computational framework for understanding delay-dependent control of oscillatory brain networks.

title: Astroglial dysfunction in models of CDKL5 deficiency disorder.
abstract: CDKL5 deficiency disorder (CDD) is a rare developmental epileptic encephalopathy typically caused by loss of function variants in the gene encoding the X-linked serine-threonine kinase CDKL5. CDKL5 is highly expressed in the brain during development, and key neuronal functions of the kinase include cytoskeletal organisation and synaptic stability. However, at present, little is known about the function of astroglia in CDD. Given the importance of these cells in synaptic development and homeostasis, as well as dysfunction in other epileptic diseases, it was hypothesised that astrocytes may contribute to CDD pathology. Induced pluripotent stem cells harbouring a CDKL5 loss-of-function mutation (and isogenic controls) were derived from CDD patient fibroblasts and differentiated into astrocytes (iAstros). Analysis of iAstros revealed transcriptomic, proteomic and functional dysregulation in CDKL5-mutant iAstros relating to water transport and immunological function, including a diminished response to TNFα stimulation. Moreover, iAstros showed increased branching and reduced phosphorylation of the known CDKL5 target end-binding protein 2 (EB2) - indicative of disrupted cytoskeletal regulation in a manner similar to CDKL5-null neurons. Finally, we report proof-of-concept of novel in vitro models of CDD. CDKL5 was knocked down in adult and foetal human organotypic brain slices through transduction with an AAV encoding a novel CDKL5 shRNA. Slices transduced with the CDKL5 shRNA displayed a trending increase in spontaneous network activity compared to those transduced with a scrambled control, demonstrating the functionality of this model. Importantly, interrogation of these models revealed dysregulation of key astrocytic proteins congruent with the human glial stem cell model. Consequently, this study describes the generation of novel human models of CDD and initial findings of astrocytic dysfunction - paving the way for novel discovery and therapeutic intervention.

title: ROCK signaling at the interface of fibrosis and neurodegeneration: mechanisms and therapeutic potential.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
abstract: Rho-associated coiled-coil containing protein kinases 1 and 2 (ROCK1 and ROCK2) regulate cytoskeletal dynamics, actomyosin contractility, extracellular matrix remodeling, and responses to mechanical stress. In the eye and central nervous system (CNS), these functions intersect with fibrocontractile scarring, neuronal dysfunction, impaired regeneration, and neuroinflammation. This review examines ROCK signaling at the interface of ocular fibrosis and neurodegeneration, emphasizing the retina as a setting in which neural injury and pathological remodeling can coexist. We outline the physiological and pathological consequences of ROCK-mediated mechanotransduction, using peripheral fibrosis only as brief comparative context, and examine its relationship with MRTF/SRF and YAP/TAZ transcriptional modules. We then assess evidence from ocular fibrotic disease, axonal regeneration, synaptic plasticity, microglial activation, and CNS injury-associated scarring, distinguishing direct ROCK-dependent mechanisms from extrapolation across tissues. ROCK1 and ROCK2 display overlapping functions with context-dependent specialization, but current evidence does not support a universal division of labor between the isoforms. Single-cell, spatial, and multi-omics approaches offer opportunities to identify disease-relevant cell populations, although transcript abundance alone cannot establish kinase activity or therapeutic dependence. Finally, we consider ocular and neural therapeutic development, including isoform-informed targeting, local delivery, and mechanism-aligned combinations. The central challenge is to suppress persistent pathological remodeling while preserving physiological repair and beneficial neural or glial responses. Resolving the cellular, spatial, and temporal requirements for ROCK signaling will be essential for testing whether antifibrotic and neuroprotective effects can be achieved together.

title: Cannabis, lived time, and the disruption of temporal self-experience.
abstract: Cannabis is the most widely used psychoactive substance subject to legal restriction worldwide, and one of its best-characterized acute effects is a distortion of the lived sense of time: users reliably report that time slows, fragments, or loses its ordinary continuity, an effect documented since the earliest controlled studies of marijuana intoxication and confirmed across decades of subsequent research. This paper argues that the relationship between cannabis use and psychopathology cannot be fully understood without attending to the phenomenology of this temporal disturbance. Drawing on the phenomenological tradition, on the clinical study of self-disorder through the Examination of Anomalous Self-Experience (EASE), and on the empirical literature on cannabis and time perception, we propose that cannabis functions as a temporal modulator whose disruptive action falls on an ipseity, or minimal self, that is itself temporally constituted. We treat the integration of a phenomenological vocabulary with an empirical, dose-response literature as a deliberate and contestable interpretive choice, which we make explicit rather than assume. Because cannabis is used across the lifespan and its subjective effects depend substantially on dose, frequency, expectation, and context, we discuss individual variability in temporal experience as a constraint on the model rather than a footnote to it. Adolescence and the clinical high-risk state are treated as one developmentally significant context for this disturbance. Reframing cannabis-related psychopathology as a disruption of lived temporality yields concrete, low-cost clinical implications: brief inquiry into the experience of time and the ownership of thought, EASE-informed assessment, and serial monitoring of self-disturbance.

title: Biophilia as a temperament trait, not a universal: children's attraction and aversion to biodiversity in the United States and Democratic Republic of Congo.
abstract: The Biophilia Hypothesis proposes that humans have a universal attraction to the natural world, yet little is known about how this attraction emerges or varies during childhood. We tested the Biophilia Reactivity Hypothesis, which reframes biophilia as an early-emerging, individually variable, temperament-like orientation toward biodiversity. We studied 295 children aged 3-13 years in two distinct settings: 124 children at the North Carolina Zoo in the United States and 171 children at Lola ya Bonobo Sanctuary in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo. Children completed a biophobia measure adapted from the Revised Fear Survey Schedule and a novel image-based biophilia task assessing Backyard Biophilia, Wildlife Tolerance, and Biophilic Travel. Children showed substantial individual variation across biophilia and biophobia measures, with responses spanning the available scale ranges. U.S. children showed higher Wildlife Tolerance and Biophilic Travel scores than Congolese children, whereas Backyard Biophilia did not differ between groups. Patterns of animal fear also differed between samples: U.S. children reported greater fear of some insects and arthropods, whereas Congolese children reported greater fear of several predators and reptiles. Biophobia was not significantly correlated with any of the three biophilia domains in either sample, indicating that low fear does not necessarily imply greater attraction to biodiversity. These findings support a model of biophilia as an individually variable, multidimensional disposition rather than a uniform human preference. They also suggest that attraction to biodiversity and fear of animals are partly distinct psychological systems and highlight the importance of studying children's biodiversity preferences across development in varying ecological and sociocultural contexts.

title: SEL1L: molecular gatekeeper of the endoplasmic reticulum quality control network.
abstract: SEL1L (suppressor/enhancer of lin-12-like) is an endoplasmic reticulum (ER) transmembrane protein that serves as a key regulatory molecule in the endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (ERAD) pathway, playing a central role in maintaining intracellular protein homeostasis. This paper provides a systematic review of SEL1L's structural characteristics, the molecular mechanisms by which it forms a functional complex with the E3 ubiquitin ligase HMG-CoA reductase degradation protein 1 (HRD1, encoded by SYVN1) to synergistically execute ERAD, and its pathophysiological significance in the onset and progression of various diseases. Research indicates that SEL1L dysfunction is closely associated with pathogenic protein aggregation in neurodegenerative diseases (e.g., Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis), protein homeostasis imbalances during tumorigenesis, cellular metabolic dysregulation in metabolic disorders (e.g., diabetes, lipid metabolism disorders), and immune system dysfunction. Furthermore, the expression levels or variants of SEL1L exhibit specific alterations across different tumor tissues, suggesting its potential as a disease biomarker and therapeutic target. This paper aims to synthesize existing research, elucidate the 'gatekeeper' role of SEL1L in multiple physiological and pathological processes, and explore the prospects for developing novel therapeutic strategies by targeting the SEL1L-HRD1 complex and related pathways.

title: Neuron-tumor communication as a target for neuromodulatory drug delivery in cancer.
abstract: Illustration of nerve-cancer interactions showing neurons, sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves, sensory neurons, and cancer-associated nerves connecting to tumor cells via synapse-like contacts, influencing cancer with neurotransmitters and signaling molecules, targeted nanoparticles, extracellular vesicles, macrophages, and CD8+ cells leading to impaired immunity.

title: Intracranial dose constraints in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma: a framework for context-specific application.
abstract: Intracranial dose constraints are often treated as fixed properties of neural tissue, yet their meaning depends on the metric, volume definition, source population and clinical time horizon in which they were derived. In IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, these conditions may differ from current planning practice. We identify three potential discontinuities: non-equivalent dose metrics may be treated as interchangeable; volume- or subregion-specific recommendations may be collapsed into single organ-level limits; and thresholds derived in longer-surviving populations may be transferred to a disease in which competing mortality may precede several late endpoints. The brainstem illustrates the metrological problem particularly clearly, whereas the hippocampus and subventricular/periventricular regions illustrate the problem of disease-specific validation. We propose a structure-specific framework with three operations: evaluation of each constraint in its source metric and anatomical definition; classification of each objective by predefined criteria of evidentiary status, endpoint severity and latency, which separates established limits from optimisation objectives; and explicit documentation of any target-coverage trade-off. No new numerical thresholds are proposed, and prognosis never justifies exceeding an established limit. Constraints protecting against severe irreversible injury, including those for the optic nerves and chiasm, are not reassessed.

title: Occupational therapy interventions for functional neurological disorder: a scoping review.
abstract: Functional Neurological Disorder (FND) is a common and disabling condition for which multidisciplinary rehabilitation is recommended; however, the specific contribution of occupational therapy remains poorly defined. This scoping review aimed to map and characterize occupational therapy interventions for people with FND, examine how these are delivered and evaluated within rehabilitation and identify priorities for future research. A scoping review was conducted using Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology. Peer-reviewed English-language intervention studies involving adults (≥18 years) with FND who received occupational therapy delivered independently or as part of multidisciplinary rehabilitation and reporting treatment outcomes were included. Descriptive analysis was undertaken. OVID Medline, Embase, APA PsycInfo and CINAHL Plus were searched from inception to July 2026, supplemented by reference list screening. Forty-one studies (n= 1,284 participants; sample sizes 1-201) were included, with only one randomized study. Occupational therapy was predominantly delivered within multidisciplinary rehabilitation; only one study included a subgroup receiving occupational therapy alone. Despite considerable variation in intervention reporting, common occupational therapy intervention components included facilitating occupational engagement, movement retraining and anxiety management, with symptom management strategies integrated into functional activities to promote confidence and independence. Improvements in symptom severity, functional ability, mental health, and quality of life were reported following multidisciplinary rehabilitation including occupational therapy. However, findings were primarily derived from uncontrolled studies, and interpretation was further limited by heterogeneity in intervention approaches, inconsistent use of outcome measures, and variable follow-up. Although occupational therapy was included in all eligible studies, occupational therapy-specific interventions and associated outcomes were inconsistently described and evaluated, limiting understanding of occupational therapy's distinct contribution within multidisciplinary rehabilitation. Future research should focus on clearly defining and evaluating the components of occupational therapy interventions.

title: Convergent molecular pathways and shared genetic mechanisms in classic syndromic autism spectrum disorders: a narrative review.
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are defined as a group of neurodevelopmental disorders that share common core features including restrictive repetitive stereotypic behavioral patterns and interests affecting social communication. Over 1,200 genes have been associated with ASD and impacted by copy number variants, chromosomal, and/or single gene defects or epigenetics. Genetic factors contribute to most cases of autism. At least twelve classic genetic disorders with autism as a common feature were selected involving 31 causative or implicated genes with 30 recognized as ASD genes. These disorders were selected to represent a range of genetic abnormalities such as chromosomal deletions, duplications, or trisomy, as well as single or multiple defective genes often with inter-relationship to other genes. Collectively, these syndromes present with neurodevelopmental/behavior/psychiatric findings with ASD, ADHD, intellectual disability and/or psychosis as features. This narrative review is novel by synthesizing available evidence on shared genes, molecular pathways, and protein-protein interaction networks across twelve classic syndromic autism spectrum disorders. Drawing on existing literature and curated web-based databases including STRING and BioGRID, nineteen of the 31 causative and/or implicated genes identified across syndromic autism disorders showed overlap across the twelve classic syndromes having different genetic defects and converged on shared molecular functions, pathways and biological processes. These related to chromatin remodeling, RNA regulation of neurodevelopment and function, synaptic signaling, neuronal connectivity, and protein homeostasis. Phelan-McDermid, Fragile X, Rett, Prader-Willi, Angelman, Burnside-Butler, and Cornelia de Lange syndromes exhibited overlapping pathways related to typical features of autism including social behavior, language acquisition, and associated neurodevelopment. Novel observations of shared molecular patterns across classic genetically distinct syndromes with ASD showed disturbances suggestive of unified, pathway-based therapeutics requiring more investigations to inform future treatment strategies.

title: Exploratory analysis of cell-free miRNA expression changes in patients with isolated first seizure and new-onset epilepsy.
abstract: One in ten individuals will experience a seizure in their lives, but only 43%-61% will be diagnosed with new-onset epilepsy (NOE). Existing methods to distinguish between a first unprovoked seizure and a diagnosis of epilepsy are inadequate and often lead to unnecessary treatment with antiseizure medications. To uncover potential targets associated with NOE, we analyzed cell-free circulating miRNA expression in plasma samples obtained from 20 patients who presented with a first unprovoked seizure. Patients were monitored for 2 years following their initial seizure, and a total of 7 patients experienced a second seizure within the follow-up period. Analysis of the miRNA expression levels revealed 15 differentially expressed miRNAs between patients who experienced only a first unprovoked seizure versus those who had a second seizure. These 15 miRNAs were experimentally linked as regulators to 160 genes related to epilepsy, including genes involved in the mTOR and WNT signaling pathways. These findings highlight a number of key circulating miRNA targets that may be further developed as a biomarker signature in larger cohorts and may offer insights into factors associated with epileptogenesis.

title: International Multicenter Retrospective Study on UBTF-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder.
abstract: UBTF encodes the upstream binding transcription factor (UBTF), a protein essential for rRNA synthesis. Dominantly acting pathogenic variants, either de novo or inherited, have been associated with a broad clinical childhood-onset neurodegenerative/neurodevelopmental spectrum whose genotype-phenotype correlation has not been accurately defined yet. This multicenter study aims to conduct a retrospective analysis of a large cohort of patients with pathogenic variants in the UBTF gene to refine diagnostic criteria and identify clinically relevant outcome measures for future trials. Clinical centers provided clinical, molecular, and neuroimaging data on patients carrying pathogenic or predicted pathogenic UBTF variants, consistent with the clinical phenotype. Data were collected using an human phenotype ontology-based standardized electronic case report form and included unreported cases or updated information on patients reported in the literature from January 2017 to December 2024. A cohort of 49 patients (23 previously unreported) was included in the study. The disease typically presented at ≤3 years (89.6%) with neuroregression in 71.4% of cases, either in a child with preexisting neurodevelopmental delay (42.9%) or after previously normal psychomotor development (28.6%). Less frequently, neurodevelopmental delay occurred in isolation (26.5%). During disease progression, patients developed behavioral abnormalities (81.6%), movement disorders (78.3%), autonomic manifestations (50.0%), and epilepsy (34.7%). At the last follow-up (mean age 13 years and 6 months), only 2 patients were deceased (4.1%). The main neuroimaging findings included white matter hyperintensity (68.1%), cerebral (66.0%) and cerebellar (51.1%) atrophy, and thinning of the corpus callosum (38.3%). However, brain MRI findings were reported as normal in 21.3% of cases. We identified 7 novel UBTF variants (c.271G>C; c.349A>T; c.495C>A; c.517G>A; c.761A>G; c.1048-2A>G; and c.1625_1626+15del). Genotype-phenotype analysis led to the distinction of 2 allelic, clinically distinct disorders: a childhood-onset neurodegenerative disease due to gain-of-function variants, characterized by the triad of neuroregression, movement, and behavioral disorders, and a neurodevelopmental disorder with a milder clinical course associated with loss-of-function/hypomorphic variants. The results from our deep-phenotyping analysis suggest the classification of UBTF-related disease into 2 main clinical syndromes impacting the natural history of the disease with a different degree of severity and complexity. This novel observation should be considered in the management and prognosis of patients and will be fundamental in the design of targeted therapies.

title: Spotsweeper-py: spatially-aware quality control metrics for spatial omics data in the Python ecosystem.
abstract: Spatially-resolved transcriptomics (SRT) generates large and heterogeneous datasets where global (tissue-wide) quality control (QC) metrics may flag large spatially contiguous regions or miss localized deviations. Recently, spatially-aware QC metrics have been introduced in SpotSweeper, but this is limited to the R programming language, which makes it challenging to use these metrics within the Python/scverse ecosystem. Here, we present SpotSweeper-py, a Python equivalent package of SpotSweeper that computes neighborhood-aware z-scores for standard QC metrics such as total counts, log total counts, number of detected genes, and percentage of mitochondrial counts. We demonstrate the performance and usability of SpotSweeper-py on two public datasets from the 10x Genomics Visium and VisiumHD platforms. This implementation of local spatially-aware QC metrics enables direct integration with Python/scverse ecosystem, reduces false positives from global quality control while preserving tissue-specific architecture. Plotting utilities are also included for quick visualizations of flagged outliers. By making robust local QC accessible in Python, SpotSweeper-py strengthens the reliability of pipelines for analyzing SRT data. The open-source software is available on PyPI ( https://pypi.org/project/spotsweeper).

title: Implementing a Belgian program to enhance the uptake and effectiveness of a multifactorial falls prevention intervention in community-dwelling older adults: A mixed-methods process and implementation evaluation.
abstract: To improve the implementation and uptake of a multifactorial falls prevention intervention, the Belgian Program to Enhance the Uptake and Effectiveness of a Multifactorial Falls Prevention Intervention in Community-Dwelling Older people (BE-EMPOWERed) program was systematically developed. It includes a 7-week group program for older people, workshops for healthcare professionals and an implementation plan with implementation guidance for primary care areas (PCAs) in Flanders. This study implemented BE-EMPOWERed in four PCAs and evaluated its implementation processes and implementation outcomes. This embedded mixed-methods process evaluation was conducted over a 2-year period in four PCAs. Implementation processes and outcomes were assessed using participant lists, fidelity checklists, observations, focus group interviews and self-reported intervention costs. The process evaluation was guided by the Medical Research Council framework. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively and qualitative data were analysed using the Qualitative Analysis Guide of Leuven. A total of 196 people participated in the group program with high attendance across sessions. Fidelity assessments across 20 group programs demonstrated high adherence to many structural and delivery-related program components. However, lower fidelity was observed for some behaviour change components. Qualitative findings suggested increased knowledge and awareness among older people, with reported application of falls prevention interventions in daily life. Overall, the findings indicate that strong engagement stemmed from group dynamics and the way group leaders delivered the program, while sustainability was hindered by limited resources and reliance on local champions. The BE-EMPOWERed program was feasible and acceptable across diverse PCAs, with high engagement and overall good fidelity. However, challenges in sustainability highlight the need for structural support to enable long-term implementation. ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06105437).

title: Variation in Enteral Feeding Practices for Very Preterm Infants in Swedish Neonatal Units: A Nationwide Survey.
abstract: To characterise enteral feeding practices in Swedish neonatal units and examine variation in practice between and within units, including adherence to local guidelines. A nationwide descriptive and exploratory web-based survey was conducted among physicians working in Swedish neonatal units caring for infants born before 32 weeks' gestation. The survey addressed prescribing practices for enteral nutrition, including feeding advancement, timing of fortification and management of selected clinical scenarios. Variation in enteral feeding practices was observed across healthcare regions, particularly regarding feeding advancement and initiation of fortification. Considerable individual variation was also observed in decision-making in common clinical scenarios, despite the presence of local guidelines. Prescribing of enteral nutrition was often described as a multidisciplinary process involving physicians, nurses and dietitians. Despite general adherence to current recommendations, substantial variation in enteral nutrition prescribing persists in Swedish neonatal units. These findings support the need for national guidelines that align with current evidence and address common clinical challenges, such as managing feeding intolerance. Given the multidisciplinary nature of enteral nutrition care and the observed individual variation, successful implementation will likely require coordinated, multidisciplinary strategies.

title: Alcohol and cardiovascular disease: inter-organ crosstalk, microvascular dysfunction, and cardiovascular ageing.
abstract: Alcohol-related cardiovascular risk is being fundamentally reappraised. Observational associations suggesting cardioprotection with light-to-moderate drinking have been challenged by contemporary cohort analyses, Mendelian-randomization studies, biomarker-informed investigations, and updated public-health guidance. Uncertainty nevertheless persists at very low exposure levels and for selected coronary or all-cause outcomes. Alcohol is therefore best viewed as a dose-, pattern-, and host-dependent cardiovascular stressor. Acute or binge drinking, sustained heavy intake, chronic intake with episodic binges, and withdrawal produce overlapping but distinct phenotypes, including hypertension, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, sudden death, alcohol-associated cardiomyopathy, heart failure, stroke, and vascular disease. A systems-cardiology framework is presented in which direct myocardial injury, electrical instability, haemodynamic and autonomic stress, vascular and microvascular dysfunction, and disrupted inter-organ signalling interact. Ethanol and acetaldehyde toxicity, redox imbalance, microbial and inflammatory mediators, neurohumoral activation, and metabolic or electrolyte disturbances can impair endothelial signalling, mitochondrial energetics, excitation-contraction coupling, electrical stability, and repair. Pathway dominance varies across exposure patterns and susceptible hosts; coronary microvascular dysfunction may represent a convergence pathway rather than an obligatory mediator. Cumulative injury can diminish perfusion, contractile, electrical, autonomic, and exercise reserve. Alcohol-related cardiovascular ageing is proposed as a unifying cumulative phenotype encompassing mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative and nitrative stress, inflammageing, senescence, impaired repair, circadian and epigenetic dysregulation, fibrosis, and ventriculo-arterial uncoupling, although direct human evidence remains incomplete. Age, biological sex, genetics, comorbidities, sleep-circadian disruption, nutrition, medications, and polysubstance misuse may modify pathway dominance and reversibility. Structured exposure assessment and alcohol reduction or abstinence, when indicated, are actionable components of cardiovascular prevention and care.

title: Human foetal cortical slice cultures: A translational platform for studying early neurodevelopment.
abstract: The developing human neocortex is characterised by complex and dynamic changes in cellular architecture, neuronal organisation and activity. We previously described how human foetal cortical organotypic slice cultures, prepared from ethically sourced tissue could be used to investigate these processes. Cultures can be maintained for weeks, exhibiting features of the normal developing brain that are not replicated in current organoid models. Such cultures allow the possibility for experimental manipulation, for instance testing the effects of genetic mutations. Here we extend the characterisation of our model. We report that these organotypic cultures preserve the laminar organisation of the developing cortical wall and show considerable diversity of neuronal morphology. Employing bulk mRNA hybridisation for 794 genes (a "human neuropathology" gene panel), we identified consistent patterns of evolving gene expression between 0 and 14 days in vitro (DIV) across different tissue samples taken at 16-18 post-conceptional weeks (pcw). To put this in the context of the normal developmental pattern, we compared our data set with previously acquired tissue RNAseq data collected between 7-17 pcw (https://www.hdbr.org/expression). This indicated that many gene expression changes in vitro followed prior developmental trajectories, but others diverged strongly, including upregulated genes associated with responses to stress, and downregulated genes associated with the vascular function. This latter effect may reflect the redundancy of vascular development in culture. Notably, various genes associated with pre- and post- synaptic function, including both glutamate and GABA receptors, continued to be expressed strongly. Consistent with this, we observed spontaneous neuronal network activity in the subplate (SP) using targeted expression of the genetically encoded Ca2+ indicator, GCaMPf6, to post-mitotic neurons. The frequency of neuronal Ca2+ transients increased when blockers of either GABAA receptors or gap junctions were applied. Conversely, activity was significantly reduced by glutamatergic receptor antagonists and abolished by voltage gated sodium channel blockade. Neuronal Ca2+ transients were triggered directly by focal application of glutamate in the SP and subventricular zone, whereas cortical plate neurons exhibited weaker responses. This was consistent with levels of immunoreactivity for glutamate receptor sub-units in these compartments. In conclusion, the organotypic cultures show functional synaptic networks, supported by continued expression of the relevant synaptic protein machinery. These data provide further validation of organotypic cultures as a model for investigating and manipulating the early prenatal development of human neocortex, a period that is otherwise difficult to study.

title: FlyAnatoView: Visualization of Drosophila Single-cell RNA-seq Datasets on Anatomographs.
abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is a powerful approach for characterizing gene expression at single-cell resolution and identifying distinct cell populations within complex tissues. However, tissue dissociation disrupts the spatial relationships among cells, making it difficult to determine their original anatomical locations and interpret gene expression patterns in the context of tissue organization. To address this limitation, we developed FlyAnatoView (https://www.flyrnai.org/tools/rna_seq_base/web/svg_files/), a resource that projects scRNA-seq data onto anatomical diagrams of Drosophila melanogaster. By integrating gene expression data with anatomical representations, FlyAnatoView helps restore spatial context and enables users to explore expression patterns across tissues, organs, and cell types. This resource provides an intuitive way to connect transcriptomic profiles with anatomical structures, facilitating the interpretation and exploration of scRNA-seq datasets.

title: Exercise Reprograms the Epigenetic-Mitochondrial Axis: Mechanisms of Healthy Aging across Muscle, Brain, and Heart.
abstract: Aging manifests as a progressive, multi-hallmark deterioration involving epigenetic dysregulation, mitochondrial impairment, proteostatic collapse, and persistent inflammaging. Accumulating evidence positions habitual physical exercise as one of the most effective non-pharmacological geroprotectors, capable of inducing beneficial, partially reversible epigenetic reprogramming across multiple tissues. This comprehensive review synthesizes current understanding of how different exercise modalitiesendurance, resistance, and high-intensity interval trainingelicit targeted changes in DNA methylation, histone posttranslational modifications, and microRNA (miRNA) networks, collectively restoring mitochondrial biogenesis, dynamics, mitophagy, and redox homeostasis in aging skeletal muscle, brain, and heart. Special emphasis is placed on the dual role of reactive oxygen species (ROS): physiological, exercise-induced ROS pulses function as pivotal redox signals that interface with AMPK-SIRT1-PGC-1α signaling, TET-mediated demethylation, Class IIa HDAC nuclear export, and miRNA maturation, thereby driving adaptive mitochondrial and proteostatic responses rather than oxidative damage. Circulating exerkines and myokines (irisin, IL-6, BDNF, apelin) further orchestrate interorgan communication, linking muscle-derived signals to hippocampal neuroplasticity and cardiac metabolic resilience. Sex-specific epigenetic patterns and differential responsiveness to exercise intensity are highlighted, revealing important sources of individual variability in geroprotective outcomes. By integrating acute versus chronic adaptive signatures and tissue-specific mechanisms, this synthesis underscores exercise as a powerful, systems-level modulator of the epigenetic-mitochondrial axis. These insights pave the way for precision exercise prescriptions and mechanistically informed mimetic strategies aimed at extending healthspan, compressing morbidity, and attenuating major age-related pathologies in heterogeneous aging populations.

title: Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) in epilepsy: Mechanistic insights from preclinical models.
abstract: Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) is a pleiotropic neuropeptide widely expressed in the central and peripheral nervous systems, with established roles in neurovascular regulation, synaptic transmission, and neuroinflammation. While CGRP has been extensively characterized in migraine pathophysiology, its role in epilepsy remains incompletely defined and is primarily supported by experimental evidence. Preclinical studies consistently demonstrate CGRP upregulation following prolonged seizures, particularly in models of status epilepticus, and suggest that CGRP signaling may contribute to key processes implicated in epileptogenesis. These include modulation of neuronal excitability, blood-brain barrier permeability, and neuroimmune responses, such as microglial activation. At the same time, CGRP has been shown to engage neuroprotective pathways, including anti-apoptotic and anti-oxidative mechanisms, as well as barrier-stabilizing effects, supporting a complex and context-dependent role. Shared pathophysiological features between migraine and epilepsy, such as cortical hyperexcitability, neuroinflammation, and cortical spreading depolarization, provide a conceptual framework in which CGRP may act as a convergent mechanistic mediator. However, direct evidence in human epilepsy remains limited, and the translational relevance of these findings requires careful interpretation. This review provides a focused synthesis of mechanistic insights from experimental models, highlighting the dual role of CGRP in seizure-related processes and delineating current gaps in knowledge. Potential clinical implications, including the effects of CGRP-targeting therapies, are discussed in a hypothesis-generating context, with emphasis on the need for rigorous studies to clarify their relevance in epilepsy. PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Migraine and epilepsy sometimes occur together and share changes in brain activity. This review examines CGRP, a signaling molecule involved in migraine, and its possible role in seizures. Animal studies suggest that CGRP can either increase abnormal brain activity and inflammation or protect nerve cells, depending on the conditions. Early observations in people raise the possibility that migraine medicines blocking CGRP could also affect seizures, but they do not prove a benefit. Further research is needed to determine whether these medicines can safely reduce seizures or prevent epilepsy.

title: Maternal responses to infant positive affect and toddler regulation of positive affect: A longitudinal pilot study.
abstract: Children's ability to regulate positive affect (PA) is a crucial yet understudied aspect of early socioemotional development. This pilot study investigated whether maternal responses to infant PA longitudinally predict toddlers' regulation of PA. Participants were 32 mother-infant dyads from a larger longitudinal study in Toronto, Canada. At 11-12 months, dyads were video recorded during naturalistic play at home. Maternal responses to infant PA were assessed using an observational coding system that distinguishes supportive (e.g., elaborative, matching) from nonsupportive (e.g., intrusive, ignoring) responses. At 18-20 months, toddlers completed the gift delay task, which measures regulation of high-arousal PA through latency to touch a desirable toy. Multiple regression analysis controlling for age and family income showed that a greater proportion of supportive responses in infancy predicted better regulation of PA in toddlerhood (β = .37, p = .027). Findings provide preliminary evidence that supportive maternal responses to PA in infancy are associated with capacities to regulate PA in toddlerhood. Results highlight the importance of examining positive as well as negative affect in models of early emotion regulation and suggest potential targets for early intervention.

title: Oral anticoagulation and cognitive outcomes in atrial fibrillation and Alzheimer's disease: considerations for longitudinal analyses.
Bridging Perceptual and Value Signal Evaluation: Meta-Analytic Evidence for the Claustrum as a Cross-Domain Integrator in Decision-Making.
abstract: Decision-making requires evaluating information across both perceptual and value domains, yet the neural mechanisms supporting this cross-domain convergence remain unclear. Using activation likelihood estimation (ALE) and meta-analytic connectivity modeling (MACM), we conducted a large-scale cross-domain meta-analysis of 90 fMRI studies involving 2564 participants to examine the neural correlates of perceptual and value signal evaluation. The results revealed partially segregated yet overlapping neural architectures for perceptual and value signal evaluation. Perceptual signal evaluation was primarily associated with a dorsal fronto-parietal-visual system, whereas value signal evaluation was mainly associated with a striato-thalamo-cingulate system. Importantly, the conjunction analysis identified the bilateral claustrum and left medial frontal gyrus as shared convergence regions across domains. MACM further showed distinguishable coactivation profiles, suggesting that these shared regions may participate in coordinating domain-specific perceptual and value-related networks rather than forming a single common decision system. Together, these findings support the claustrum as a candidate domain-general integrator that may bridge sensory, motivational, and executive processes, providing a cross-domain account of decision-making.

title: Altered Sensory and Affective Inflammatory Pain Responding in the VPA Model of Autism Is Associated With Reduced IL1β-NLRP3 Expression in the ACC in Males but Not Females.
abstract: Prenatal valproic acid (VPA) exposure, a well-validated preclinical model of autism, is associated with altered sensory responding to noxious heat and mechanical stimuli. However, whether sensory and affective responding to inflammatory noxious stimuli are altered, and whether effects are sex-specific is unknown. Neuroimmune crosstalk in the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) modulates sensory and affective dimensions of pain and may contribute to altered pain in autism. This study examined acute and chronic inflammatory pain responding following intraplantar formalin or complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA) in male and female VPA-exposed rats, and associated gene changes in the ACC. VPA-exposed male and female rats exhibited heat and mechanical hyposensitivity, with no change in responses to innocuous cold. Nociceptive responding in the formalin test was unaltered; however, following CFA administration, VPA-exposed rats displayed higher mechanical, but not cold, withdrawal thresholds compared with saline counterparts. VPA-exposed rats showed higher paw withdrawal latencies in the Hargreaves' test following CFA, with effects influenced by sex and time. VPA-exposed males exhibited reduced anxiety-like behavior in the open field test following CFA and reduced affective/aversive pain behavior in the PEAP test prior to and following CFA administration, effects not observed in females. In male VPA-exposed rats, CFA-induced mechanical hypersensitivity and aversive-like behavior were associated with reduced Il1b and Nlrp3 expression in the ACC. These data demonstrate that prenatal VPA exposure alters nociceptive and chronic inflammatory pain responding and suggest that sex-specific neuroimmune alterations in the ACC may play a central role in these effects. Pain in autism is poorly understood and challenging to manage. This study shows sex-dependent changes in chronic inflammatory pain responding and associated alterations in neuroimmune gene expression in the ACC in an autism-relevant preclinical model. These findings highlight neuroimmune signalling as a potential contributor to atypical pain processing in autism and an important avenue for future translational pain research.

title: Resting-State Hyper- and Hypo-Connectivity in Early Schizophrenia: Which Tip of the Iceberg to Focus On?
abstract: We examine brain connectivity alterations in early-stage schizophrenia, with a focus on patterns of hyper- and hypoconnectivity. Although altered functional connectivity (FC) is well documented in schizophrenia, substantial inconsistencies remain regarding the location and direction of specific dysconnections. We hypothesize that early FC changes in schizophrenia include both decreases and increases and are correlated with symptoms and medication levels, with insufficient preprocessing potentially masking out some of these effects. Using a large sample of 100 first-episode schizophrenia patients (42 females) and 90 healthy controls (50 females), we compared FC across 90 brain regions defined by the Automated Anatomical Labeling atlas. We assessed medication effects and examined associations between FC changes and duration of untreated psychosis, duration of antipsychotic (AP) treatment, and symptom severity. In addition, we performed a systematic comparison of four functional magnetic resonance imaging data denoising strategies. Relative to controls, patients showed increased FC in 150 region pairs and decreased FC in 15 pairs, when using a "stringent" data denoising scheme. Despite this numerical imbalance, the overall distribution of FC changes remained balanced: Median FC was not systematically shifted, indicating no global bias toward hyper- or hypoconnectivity. Importantly, several FC alterations were significantly associated with symptom severity and AP medication. These findings indicate localized dysconnections embedded within a globally balanced connectivity profile in early schizophrenia. This balance was disrupted by less stringent denoising, leading to results dominated by hypoconnectivity, highlighting preprocessing as a major source of variability across studies.

title: Harmonization of Longitudinal Multi-Scanner Neuroimaging Data With Nonlinear Biological Associations.
abstract: The aggregation of neuroimaging data across multiple sources, typically scanners or imaging sites, has the potential to improve statistical power when conducting inference. The added benefits of increased sample size to inference, however, can be obstructed by unwanted source-specific technical variability that increases difficulty in estimating biological signals of interest. To address this issue, recent methods based on ComBat, a batch-correction procedure originally developed for genomics, have been developed for both cross-sectional and longitudinal neuroimaging data. While these approaches have successfully removed technical batch-specific variability, they restrict their consideration to linear biological associations. In this article we introduce a ComBat-based method to harmonize longitudinal multisource imaging data that can account for nonlinear biological associations of interest. We demonstrate via simulation that, in the presence of nonlinear biological signal, our method outperforms existing ComBat-based approaches designed for longitudinal imaging data, particularly in settings where observed values of relevant biological covariates lack substantial overlap across sources. Using volumetric measurements for 504 subjects combined from both the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging (BLSA) and the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), we identify the presence of both additive and multiplicative study-specific effects for a substantial number of brain regions and demonstrate the effective removal of their presence on data harmonized by our method. The flexibility of the proposed method towards capturing many types of biological associations makes it a versatile procedure that can be used to harmonize longitudinal biomedical data.

title: Treatment-Induced Neuropathy of Diabetes: Clinical Insights from a Case Series and Systematic Review.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Treatment-induced neuropathy of diabetes (TIND) is an under-recognized iatrogenic neuropathy that follows a rapid fall in glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c). We aimed to systematically summarize the published cases of TIND and to compare them with two patients evaluated at our center. Methods: We evaluated two patients at our center and systematically reviewed PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar, following PRISMA 2020, for primary clinical studies of TIND. Data were synthesized descriptively. Results: Both patients developed painful neuropathy with autonomic symptoms after HbA1c falls of 15.3 and 6.4 percentage points and improved substantially, but incompletely, over two years. Moreover, the review included 47 publications (219 patients) and painful neuropathy with autonomic dysfunction predominated. In case reports, the median HbA1c fall was 7.3 percentage points, and onset occurred within 8 weeks in 26 of 47 publications. Recovery was complete in 8 and partial in 21 of 32 case reports with documented outcomes. Follow-up data were missing for 136 of 219 patients. Conclusions: Published cases show a recurrent temporal association between TIND and rapid HbA1c reduction, but cannot establish causality or prognosis. TIND should be recognized early, and gradual, monitored glycemic correction may be reasonable in high-risk patients.

title: Self-Reported Handicap and Pain in Multiple Sclerosis: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of the London Handicap Scale and Disability Status in a Slovak Neurorehabilitation Cohort.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Handicap (participation restriction) and pain are clinically important but under-investigated outcomes in multiple sclerosis (MS). We examined the London Handicap Scale (LHS) and pain (Visual Analogue Scale, VAS) in relation to disability and other clinical variables. Methods: This secondary, cross-sectional, non-interventional analysis included 65 Slovak patients with MS (study group, SG, n = 32, designated for a 12-week neurorehabilitation program; control group, CG, n = 33, waitlisted), all assessed before rehabilitation. Associations were tested with Spearman correlation (Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted) and linear regression; groups were compared with the Mann-Whitney test. Results: Disability (EDSS) correlated with LHS (ρ = -0.667) and VAS pain (ρ = 0.457; both p < 0.001), although SF-36 measures correlated more strongly. In adjusted models, EDSS was the only significant predictor, explaining 44.1% of the variance in LHS and 21.1% in VAS pain. LHS and VAS pain did not differ between SG and CG (p = 0.936 and p = 0.770) but differed across EDSS severity subgroups (p < 0.001 and p = 0.007). Conclusions: EDSS is a significant but partial correlate of handicap and pain, supporting their assessment alongside disability staging. The baseline group comparison is descriptive and provides no evidence about the effects of neurorehabilitation.

title: Bone Health in Children and Adolescents with Sex Chromosome Aneuploidies: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Sex chromosome aneuploidies (SCAs)-including Turner syndrome, Klinefelter syndrome, Trisomy X (47,XXX), and 47,XYY (Jacobs) syndrome-are among the most common chromosomal conditions in humans. The available evidence on skeletal health in SCAs is heterogeneous and varies substantially across conditions. Although skeletal abnormalities and increased fracture risk are well documented in Turner syndrome, pediatric evidence in Klinefelter syndrome and Trisomy X remains limited, while dedicated skeletal data for 47,XYY are essentially absent. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on bone health in children and adolescents with the major SCAs. Methods: A structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library was conducted, supplemented by backward and forward citation tracking. Pediatric studies were prioritized, while adult and mechanistic studies were included when necessary to address evidence gaps. Owing to the narrative design, no formal risk-of-bias assessment or quantitative synthesis was performed. Results: Pediatric evidence is most extensive for Turner syndrome, in which fracture risk and bone mineral status are influenced by ovarian insufficiency, growth, body size, comorbidities, and treatment exposure. Direct pediatric skeletal evidence for Klinefelter syndrome and Trisomy X remains limited and heterogeneous, deriving from small observational studies and, for Klinefelter syndrome, a randomized interventional trial. Dedicated data for 47,XYY syndrome are essentially absent. Interpretation of dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry requires particular attention to short stature, tall stature, and pubertal delay. Conclusions: Clinical assessment should be individualized, with attention to endocrine and nutritional factors, appropriate interpretation of bone imaging, and promotion of bone-healthy lifestyle measures. Further prospective pediatric studies are needed to clarify fracture risk, monitoring strategies, and treatment effects across SCAs.

title: Distribution of Pathological Entities and Surgical Procedures Across Cervical Levels in Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy: An Exploratory Single-Center Analysis.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Surgical planning in degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM) considers the type of pathology, the number of levels involved, and cervical alignment and stability, but how the pathological entity, the operated level, and the procedure performed relate to one another remains unclear. This study described their distribution and associations in a consecutive surgical cohort. Methods: A total of 154 consecutive adults operated for DCM at a single center between 2013 and 2024 were studied retrospectively. Six non-mutually-exclusive pathological entities, five procedure types and every operated level (C2-C3 to T1-T2) were recorded, with combined procedures counted once. Associations were tested with Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact tests, with sensitivity analyses using a single dominant entity per patient and patient-level clustering, and a comparison of patients treated by ACDF alone versus any alternative strategy. Results: Procedure selection was related to the pathological entity (p < 0.001): isolated disc herniation was treated almost exclusively with ACDF (93.2%), whereas spondylolisthesis was the most heterogeneous, managed with posterior decompression and fixation (33.3%), ACCF (23.3%) or ACDF (23.3%); this persisted in the dominant-entity analysis (p = 0.002). The 46 patients (29.9%) not treated by ACDF alone were older, had more operated levels, worse baseline mJOA and more often circumferential compression (all p ≤ 0.005), whereas sagittal profile and cord and canal morphometry did not differ.
