Neither entities nor procedures were associated with the operated level across C3-C7 (p = 0.84 and p = 0.93); a nominally significant all-level result (p = 0.008) arose only from the sparsely operated terminal levels. Conclusions: Procedure selection in DCM was driven mainly by the underlying pathological entity, disease extent and compression geometry, rather than by the operated level or cervical alignment. No outcome data were analyzed, so these descriptive, hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in larger multicenter cohorts with adequate representation of the terminal levels.

title: Pregabalin and α2δ Subunit Modulation: A Systematic Review of Preclinical Evidence for Intraocular Pressure Regulation and Retinal Neuroprotection.
abstract: Background: Glaucoma is a multifactorial optic neuropathy characterized by progressive retinal ganglion cell (RGC) loss, in which both intraocular pressure (IOP)-dependent and -independent mechanisms contribute to disease progression. Gabapentinoids target α2δ subunits of voltage-gated calcium channels (VGCCs), which regulate calcium-dependent processes relevant to both aqueous humor dynamics and retinal neuronal function. This systematic review evaluates heterogeneous evidence relevant to α2δ modulation of IOP regulation, retinal neuroprotection, and associated molecular and synaptic pathways. Methods: A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Library databases from inception. Studies investigating gabapentinoids or α2δ subunit modulation with outcomes related to IOP, RGC survival, or relevant molecular signaling were included. Risk of Bias (RoB) was assessed using the OHAT rating tool, and Certainty of Evidence (CoE) was rated on the GRADE four-level scale using initial confidence criteria from the OHAT approach. Due to heterogeneity in study design and outcomes, findings were synthesized narratively, with included studies divided and assessed separately within anterior segment pharmacology, anterior segment genetics, neuroprotection, and mechanistic bodies of evidence. Results: Of 1973 unique records screened, 11 studies met inclusion criteria, which were further subdivided into 15 experimental arms according to evidence type. Distinct evidence bodies were anterior segment pharmacology (5 study arms), anterior segment genetics (3 study arms), neuroprotection (4 study arms), and mechanistic (3 study arms). Across mouse and rabbit models of spontaneous ocular hypertension, topical pregabalin (PRG) consistently reduced IOP in a dose-dependent manner, with peak effects generally occurring 1.5-5 h after administration depending on strain and formulation. Plateaus in maximal IOP reduction were observed at 0.9% PRG solution in mice and 0.6-0.7% PRG microemulsion (ME) in rabbits. ME formulations of PRG consistently prolonged duration of action and increased cumulative exposure relative to non-ME PRG formulations. PRG ME achieved maximal IOP reduction comparable to that of 0.005% latanoprost solution while retaining their increased duration of action and cumulative exposure. Repeated once-daily PRG ME dosing maintained IOP-lowering responses over 21- and 60-day treatment periods. Genetic studies separately associated CACNA2D1/Cacna2d1 with IOP-related phenotypes and primary open-angle glaucoma susceptibility, providing target-level evidence. Preclinical posterior segment studies reported retinal structural preservation or improved RGC survival with PRG, while separate studies of GBP-L demonstrated RGC-survival effects associated with K-ATP channel activity rather than established α2δ modulation. Mechanistic studies separately identified thrombospondin-2 (TSP2)-α2δ1 signaling as a mediator of injury-associated synaptic remodeling, with pharmacologic disruption attenuating synaptic protein upregulation and improving axonal integrity. RoB varied across study arms and bodies of evidence. Anterior pharmacology included five Tier II study arms, anterior genetics included two Tier I arms and one Tier II arm, and all neuroprotection and mechanistic arms were Tier II. CoE was rated moderate for both anterior pharmacology and genetics, and low for both neuroprotection and mechanistic evidence. Conclusions: The available evidence is predominantly preclinical and heterogeneous. Moderate certainty within the defined anterior segment evidence body reflects consistency of the reported preclinical effect and does not establish clinical efficacy or independent reproducibility, as the topical PRG intervention literature is concentrated within a single investigative group. The neuroprotective and mechanistic findings remain hypothesis-generating and do not establish a unified mechanism or simultaneous IOP-lowering and neuroprotective action. Independent pharmacologic replication, validation in chronic glaucomatous neurodegeneration models, and long-term topical safety evaluation are prerequisites to discussions of clinical relevance.

title: Clinical and Economic Burdens of ADHD Across Developmental Stages: A Review.
abstract: Background: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder that can persist across the lifespan and is associated with substantial clinical, economic, and psychosocial burden. This narrative review examines the clinical and economic burdens of ADHD on individuals and families, encompassing direct medical costs, including assessment and treatment expenditures, alongside non-medical costs, educational and occupational disruption, caregiving demands, and adverse mental health outcomes among family members. It synthesizes evidence across developmental stages and geographic regions and considers the clinical implications of these interconnected burdens. Methods: A structured search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase, supplemented by reference-list screening, identified English-language publications from January 2000 through June 2026. Evidence was synthesized narratively across direct medical, non-medical, and family-related burdens, prioritizing large population-based and administrative claims studies, longitudinal investigations, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses. Interpretation considered study design, confounding factors, economic perspectives, and differences in cost estimation. Results: ADHD is associated with substantial healthcare, non-medical, and family-related economic costs. Reported costs encompass diagnostic assessment, treatment, comorbidity, and adverse events, alongside educational support, occupational losses, accidents, and criminal justice involvement. Families experience reduced occupational productivity, elevated caregiving demands, greater healthcare utilization, and increased depression, anxiety, and stress. Conclusions: Clinically, these findings support assessing functional and family-level burden alongside symptoms, identifying and managing comorbidities, maintaining treatment during transitions to adult services, and monitoring tolerability. Integrating these burden domains into routine assessment and treatment planning may help identify modifiable drivers of impairment and guide more comprehensive care across the lifespan for patients and their families.

title: When "Normal" Hemoglobin May Not Be Enough: Sex-Specific Anemia Thresholds and Outcomes in Cardiac Surgery.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Sex-specific anemia criteria classify women with hemoglobin (Hb) 12.0-12.9 g/dL as non-anemic. We assessed whether World Health Organization (WHO) criteria underrecognize red blood cell (RBC) transfusion risk compared with a uniform patient blood management (PBM) threshold of Hb <13.0 g/dL in elective open cardiac valve surgery (CVS). Methods: This nationwide retrospective cohort included adults undergoing elective open CVS in 40 Spanish centers (2016-2024), 32 of which reported preoperative Hb. Hb was modeled continuously and in three strata (<12.0, 12.0-12.9, ≥13.0 g/dL). The primary outcome was RBC transfusion; secondary outcomes were postoperative complications, length of stay, and in-hospital mortality within 30 days. Mixed-effects models adjusted for age, comorbidity burden, surgical complexity, valve position, year of surgery, and center. Results: Among 29,757 eligible patients, 20,017 had available Hb measurements; 9247 (46.2%) were women, including 2333 (25.2%) with Hb 12.0-12.9 g/dL. In this stratum, 68.0% of women and 52.7% of men received RBC transfusions. The adjusted between-sex probability difference was 15.1 percentage points (95% CI, 11.4-18.9; adjusted odds ratio, 1.85; 95% CI, 1.59-2.16). The categorical sex × Hb interaction was significant (p < 0.001), whereas the continuous interaction was not (p = 0.486). Sex did not significantly modify the Hb associations with complications or in-hospital mortality within 30 days. Conclusions: Women with Hb 12.0-12.9 g/dL had substantial transfusion risk despite being classified as non-anemic by the WHO criteria. Hb <13.0 g/dL may be a pragmatic sex-inclusive trigger for perioperative risk recognition and etiologic evaluation, not a proven therapeutic target.

title: Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation Combined with General Anesthesia in Minimally Invasive Surgery for Lung Cancer: A Randomized, Patient- and Assessor-Blinded, Sham-Controlled Trial.
abstract: Background: We aimed to clarify (1) the analgesic efficacy of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) combined with general anesthesia during minimally invasive lung cancer surgery and (2) exploratory neural network correlates of acupuncture-drug combined anesthesia. Methods: Eligible patients receiving general anesthesia for minimally invasive lung cancer surgery were randomly allocated to perioperative TEAS or sham-TEAS in this randomized, patient- and assessor-blinded, sham-controlled trial. Postoperative patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) was administered. Outcome measures included postoperative visual analog scale (VAS) pain scores, sufentanil consumption via PCIA, and total/effective PCIA pump presses. Perioperative electroencephalography (EEG) was acquired using a 22-lead recorder, and brainwave power spectra were analyzed using Fourier transform. Repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA) was applied to serial postoperative VAS scores at 6, 24 and 48 h. Independent-samples t-tests compared cumulative sufentanil consumption at 6, 24 and 48 h postoperatively. Post hoc simple-effect comparisons were performed as exploratory analyses without multiplicity adjustment. The EEG sub-study was exploratory; false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction was used to control multiple comparisons across electrodes and frequency bands. Results: In total, 109 patients were randomized. A significant group-by-time interaction was detected for postoperative VAS scores (F(1.599,171.124) = 68.287, p < 0.001). Simple-effect analyses revealed lower VAS scores in the TEAS group at postoperative 6 h (mean difference -1.900, 95%CI -2.181 to -1.619, p < 0.001) and 24 h (mean difference -1.391, 95%CI -1.645 to -1.138, p < 0.001), with no between-group difference at 48 h (mean difference -0.066, 95%CI -0.320 to 0.187, p = 0.605). The TEAS group also exhibited reduced PCIA sufentanil consumption at 6, 24 and 48 h postoperatively, alongside fewer total and effective PCIA pump presses. After FDR correction, exploratory EEG analysis identified potential dipole-related power differences in the prefrontal, occipital, parietal (postcentral gyrus), temporal and diencephalic regions, predominantly within beta-band oscillations (14-35 Hz). Conclusions: These exploratory findings suggest that TEAS combined with general anesthesia may reduce postoperative pain and analgesic requirement. This potential benefit may arise from TEAS-mediated modulation of pain-related neural networks; however, the observed intraoperative EEG oscillatory differences are exploratory neurophysiological correlates and do not confirm causal mechanisms.

title: Long Life but High Suicide Rates in Sardinia's Blue Zone: Evidence That Major Depression Alone May Not Explain the Paradox.
abstract: Background: The Sardinian Blue Zone is internationally recognized for exceptional longevity, particularly among men. The provinces encompassing this area also report elevated suicide mortality among older men. This paradox raises the question of whether older men recruited within the longevity area show increased depressive screening positivity or whether additional interacting mechanisms may contribute to suicide vulnerability. Objective: To examine whether the reported excess suicide mortality among older men in the provinces encompassing the Sardinian Blue Zone is accompanied by higher depressive screening positivity or PHQ-9 Item 9 scores in older men recruited within the longevity area, and to explore the distribution of subthreshold depressive symptoms. Methods: We conducted an exploratory secondary analysis of a population-based survey including Sardinian residents aged ≥60 years. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). The Blue Zone group was recruited from six municipalities within the longevity area in Nuoro and Ogliastra. Comparisons were stratified by sex and used two-sided Fisher exact tests and analysis of variance. Results: No statistically significant increase in screening positivity for probable depression or PHQ-9 Item 9 scores was observed in Blue Zone residents. Older men showed a higher prevalence of clinically relevant symptoms below the screening threshold for probable major depression (PHQ-9 5-9: 4/19 vs. 4/171; OR = 11.13; Fisher p = 0.00395). Among women, this symptom range was less frequent in the Blue Zone (5/34 vs. 77/208; Fisher p = 0.01077). Conclusions: The observed symptom distributions motivate examination of mechanisms extending beyond the prevalence of major depression alone. The male excess in subthreshold depressive symptoms, interpreted alongside independent evidence on activation, supports investigation of mood and rhythm dysregulation and culturally shaped responses to stress. The sociobiological framework generates testable hypotheses for longitudinal psychiatric and anthropological research.

title: Image-Guided TIVAP by Interventional Radiologists: A Single-Center Cohort Study Using Institutional Surgical Benchmarks.
abstract: Background/Objectives: To evaluate the resource utilization, procedural costs, procedure time, and intraprocedural outcomes of interventional radiology (IR)-guided totally implantable venous access port (TIVAP) placement and contextualize these findings using institutional surgical benchmarks. Methods: We conducted a single-center study between March 2020 and March 2024 that included 93 patients requiring TIVAP placement for chemotherapy. All ports were inserted under ultrasound and fluoroscopic guidance in an angiography suite. Surgical insertions using a cephalic vein cut-down under anesthesia were used as a comparator. Data collected included number of consent forms, staffing, procedure duration, material and medication utilization, and procedural costs obtained from hospital financial records. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize outcomes. Results: IR-guided TIVAP insertion required one combined consent form and two personnel, compared with two consent forms and four personnel for the surgical workflow. The average procedural cost in the angiography suite was €168.16 versus an institutional surgical benchmark of €407.90, representing a 58.8% lower observed cost. The recorded average procedure time was 45 min for IR versus 85 min for the surgical benchmark. Material costs were comparable, except for intravenous anesthetic agents used in the operating room. No intraprocedural complications occurred among the 93 IR cases. Conclusions: IR-guided TIVAP implantation required fewer personnel and was associated with lower observed procedural costs and shorter recorded procedure times relative to institutional surgical benchmarks. The absence of a patient-level surgical comparator and long-term follow-up limits conclusions regarding comparative safety and clinical outcomes.

title: Cardioprotection and Heart Failure Management in Duchenne and Becker Muscular Dystrophies: A State-of-the-Art Review Across Pediatric and Transitional Age.
abstract: Advances in respiratory care have significantly extended the life expectancy of patients with Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophies (DMD/BMD), making progressive dilated cardiomyopathy the leading cause of mortality in this population. Historically, a conservative "watch and wait" approach was often maintained until overt systolic dysfunction became evident. However, the advent of advanced echocardiographic technologies, particularly Global Longitudinal Strain (GLS) imaging, has demonstrated that myocardial impairment begins in early childhood, long before a decline in ejection fraction occurs. This critical evidence strongly advocates for a paradigm shift toward early, proactive cardioprotective strategies. As patients progress into the transitional age and adulthood, the pediatric prophylactic approach (traditionally based on ACE inhibitors and beta-blockers) must integrate with evolving adult heart failure guidelines. This comprehensive review critically evaluates the pathophysiological continuum of dystrophic cardiomyopathy. We highlight the prognostic value of early subclinical detection (GLS) and specifically discuss the transition to modern guideline-directed medical therapies (GDMTs), exploring the emerging role of Angiotensin Receptor-Neprilysin Inhibitors (ARNI, e.g., sacubitril/valsartan) and SGLT2 inhibitors (e.g., dapagliflozin) in this specific cohort. Finally, we address the role of advanced device therapies (ICD, CRT, and left ventricular assist devices) in end-stage disease. By bridging pediatric neurology and adult cardiology, this review aims to equip clinicians with an updated, multidisciplinary framework to optimize cardiovascular outcomes in the growing population of transitional-age DMD/BMD patients.

title: Awareness, Attitudes and Self-Reported Practices Regarding Perinatal Mental Health and Depression Screening Among Healthcare Professionals in Serbia: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Survey.
abstract: Background: Mood disorders, especially perinatal depression (PND), are a major public health concern, yet in Serbia there are no standardized screening protocols and limited data on healthcare professionals' preparedness to recognize and manage it. Aims: To explore awareness, attitudes toward screening, self-reported familiarity, and self-reported clinical practices regarding PND among healthcare professionals in Serbia. Method: A cross-sectional, anonymous online survey was conducted in a convenience sample of 221 healthcare professionals (gynecology/obstetrics, pediatrics, psychiatry, midwifery, and community nursing) from two urban centers (Belgrade and Niš). A de novo 23-item survey was used. Group differences were tested with Fisher's exact tests, and associations with demographic and professional characteristics were examined with penalized (Firth) logistic and ordinal regression models with psychiatry as reference category; p-values were Holm-adjusted within each family of tests. Results: Most respondents recognized pregnancy (85.5%) and the postpartum period (93.7%) as periods of increased risk for mental disorders and supported routine screening (91.0%). However, self-reported awareness of guidelines, screening timeframes, and diagnostic criteria was limited, particularly among non-psychiatric professionals. In multivariable analyses using psychiatry as the reference category, respondents working in gynecology/obstetrics had significantly lower odds of reporting awareness of national guidelines (OR = 0.120, 95% CI 0.038-0.327), international guidelines (OR = 0.176, 95% CI 0.044-0.575), recommended screening timeframes (OR = 0.053, 95% CI 0.007-0.237), and institutional clinical pathways (OR = 0.047, 95% CI 0.005-0.235). Respondents working in pediatrics also had lower odds of reporting awareness of national guidelines (OR = 0.121, 95% CI 0.043-0.297) and screening timeframes (OR = 0.032, 95% CI 0.005-0.132). Both non-psychiatric groups had higher odds of reporting poorer familiarity with ICD-10 diagnostic criteria and choosing referral to a psychiatrist rather than initiating screening themselves in the clinical vignette. All reported associations remained significant after Holm correction. Conclusions: In this convenience sample, gaps in self-reported familiarity, screening practices, and perceived institutional organization were evident, particularly outside psychiatry. Although the findings cannot be extrapolated to the national level without caution, they suggest that integrating routine screening into maternal care, targeted training, and updated national guidelines could improve the early detection and care of PND.

title: Recalculated HOMA-IR and Recorded Blood Pressure Changes in Treated Internal Medicine Patients: An Exploratory Retrospective Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: In treated patients, concurrent metabolic and blood pressure (BP) changes are difficult to interpret without complete treatment histories. We examined the association between change in homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) and systolic BP (SBP), and described trajectories by prescribed management category. Methods: This exploratory retrospective cohort included 150 patients (132 inpatients and 18 outpatients at baseline), with visits labeled baseline, month 3, and month 6; exact dates were unavailable. Four nonrandomized categories were compared by baseline prescription, without adherence data. HOMA analyses excluded two participants with explicit insulin entries; complete-case regression used heteroscedasticity-consistent (HC3) confidence intervals (CIs). Results: The principal SBP coefficient was 2.20 mmHg per HOMA-IR doubling (95% CI -1.90 to 6.31; n = 99). Restrictions to no recorded baseline diabetes (n = 71) or no pharmacological glucose-lowering entry (n = 77) also yielded imprecise estimates. SBP decreased by 2.07-8.23 mmHg across prescribed categories, but adjusted contrasts were uncertain (global p = 0.743). The waist-SBP coefficient did not meet the multiplicity criterion (q = 0.107). Of 724 recorded BP values, 720 were multiples of 5 mmHg. Conclusions: The association between HOMA-IR change and recorded SBP change remained uncertain, and the efficacy of prescribed diet or omega-3 supplementation could not be assessed. The principal contribution of the study is to show how incompletely documented medication exposure, adherence, visit timing, and measurement conditions limit the interpretation of serial HOMA-IR and routine BP values in treated patients.

title: Choriocapillaris Alterations in Type 1 and Type 2 Torpedo Maculopathy: A Multimodal Imaging Case Series.
abstract: Background: Torpedo maculopathy is an uncommon, usually asymptomatic chorioretinal lesion temporal to the fovea. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) distinguishes a non-cavitary type 1 from a cavitary type 2 phenotype, but choriocapillaris involvement in these phenotypes remains incompletely defined. This report describes the choriocapillaris findings in one patient with each phenotype. Methods: Two women with unilateral torpedo maculopathy, aged 18 (type 1) and 52 years (type 2), underwent multicolor imaging, fundus autofluorescence, spectral-domain OCT, and OCT angiography, which were assessed qualitatively. Results: Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes of each patient. Both lesions showed outer-retinal changes and topographic correspondence between fundus autofluorescence abnormalities and choriocapillaris flow-signal attenuation. In the type 1 lesion, the inner retinal layers were preserved without cavitation, and choriocapillaris attenuation was focal and relatively homogeneous. The type 2 lesion showed subretinal cavitation (subretinal cleft), focal attenuation of the retinal pigment epithelium-Bruch membrane complex, and a choriocapillaris flow deficit that appeared more extensive within the imaged region. Conclusions: These observations suggest involvement of the retinal pigment epithelium-choriocapillaris unit in both phenotypes. As they derive from one patient per phenotype at a single time point, they cannot be extended to the two subtypes; longitudinal imaging is required to define the temporal relationship between outer-retinal and choriocapillaris changes.

title: Lateral Epicondylalgia as a Nociceptive/Nociplastic Pain Condition According to the International Association for the Study of Pain (IASP) Taxonomy: A Theoretical Hypothesis.
abstract: Lateral epicondylalgia (LE) is a chronic musculoskeletal pain condition characterized by treatment effect heterogeneity. The identification of specific pain phenotypes may help in subgrouping LE patients based on their predominant pain mechanism, thereby supporting the development of more targeted treatments. In the current proposal, we present a conceptual application of the International Association for the Study of Pain (IASP) taxonomy to identify a predominant LE pain phenotype. The clinical presentation of LE is traditionally considered predominantly nociceptive, with the wrist extensor tendon as the main peripheral driver. Thus, the presence of trigger point (TrP)-associated referred pain has also been considered as a potential peripheral nociceptive drive. However, the treatment of peripheral drivers alone has shown limited short-term effects in LE, requiring research beyond possible peripheral inputs. Furthermore, evidence supports the presence of altered pain processing in some individuals with LE, suggestive of nociplastic pain features in a subgroup of patients. The potential presence of nociplastic features would imply the need to address maladaptive neuroplasticity associated with pain processing in these patients with LE. The current proposal hypothesizes that LE is a heterogeneous pain condition in which different pain phenotypes, e.g., nociceptive-alone, nociplastic, or mixed-type, can coexist in some patients with different relevance according to the duration, intensity, stage and severity of the disease. Recognizing the relative predominance of nociceptive and nociplastic phenotypes may guide more individualized treatment selection in individuals with LE. However, these hypotheses require prospective validation before they can be established as a clinical decision-making tool. Future studies should identify high-value care options for the treatment of people with LE, as current approaches only yield short-term effects.

title: Management of Facial Nerve Paresis After Nerve-Preserving Parotidectomy: A Review.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Postoperative facial nerve paresis remains clinically relevant after nerve-preserving parotidectomy. This scoping review aimed to identify, map, and characterize reported therapeutic strategies and summarize clinical recovery outcomes. Methods: Following Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and PRISMA-ScR, the protocol was deposited on Figshare before data extraction. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched through 24 August 2026. English-language original studies of treatments initiated after the recognition of paresis were eligible. Two reviewers independently selected and appraised studies; one reviewer charted the data and another verified the extraction. Results: Eight studies involving 211 patients were included; reported ages were 17-86 years. Procedures included partial, superficial, subtotal, total, and revision parotidectomy, as well as parotid lobectomy for benign or malignant disease. Immediate or early weakness predominated; two reports described delayed-onset palsy. Evidence comprised two randomized trials, one case-control study, one multicenter cohort, and four case reports. Interventions included corticosteroids, corticosteroid-antiviral therapy, home or supervised exercises, Kabat rehabilitation, neuromuscular retraining, Matrix Rhythm Therapy (MRT), and proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation with electrical stimulation. The trials found no benefit of prednisolone over placebo and no statistically significant difference between supervised rehabilitation and home exercises; equivalence was not established. Observational findings could not be separated from spontaneous recovery or co-treatment. Conclusions: No intervention has established superiority. Standardized protocols, validated outcomes, and adequately powered comparative studies are needed.

title: Association Between Daily Energy Intake and Cognitive Recovery After Mechanical Thrombectomy for Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
abstract: Background: Post-stroke cognitive impairment is a common complication associated with reduced functional independence and quality of life. Although adequate daily energy intake is considered an essential component of stroke rehabilitation, its association with cognitive recovery after mechanical thrombectomy remains poorly understood. This study investigated the relationship between daily energy intake and 90-day cognitive outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke treated with mechanical thrombectomy. Methods: This multicenter retrospective observational cohort study included 100 consecutive patients undergoing mechanical thrombectomy between 1 April 2025 and 1 April 2026 at stroke centers in the United Kingdom and Romania. Daily energy and macronutrient intake were retrospectively extracted from routine clinical records and normalized to body weight (kcal/kg/day). Daily energy intake was evaluated primarily as a continuous exposure (kcal/kg/day), while the originally defined 31 kcal/kg/day grouping was retained for exploratory categorical analyses. Cognitive performance was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) at baseline and, among survivors with available cognitive follow-up, at 90 days. The primary multivariable model evaluated daily energy intake (kcal/kg/day) as a continuous exposure and adjusted for baseline MoCA, atrial fibrillation, chronic coronary artery disease, admission NIHSS, C-reactive protein, and PICA/AICA/SCA occlusion. HC3 heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors were used for robust inference. Results: Among patients with available 90-day cognitive assessment, those with higher energy intake achieved significantly higher 90-day MoCA scores than those with lower intake (24.2 ± 2.1 vs. 20.0 ± 1.5; p < 0.001) and greater cognitive improvement (ΔMoCA: 3.82 ± 1.08 vs. 0.48 ± 0.54 points; p < 0.001). In the primary continuous-exposure model, each additional 1 kcal/kg/day was associated with a 0.18-point higher 90-day MoCA score after multivariable adjustment (β = 0.179, HC3 95% CI 0.081-0.278; p < 0.001). The association remained similar in an expanded sensitivity model addressing available indicators of baseline severity (β = 0.176, HC3 95% CI 0.071-0.281; p = 0.002). Exploratory categorical analyses also showed higher 90-day MoCA scores in the higher-intake group. No significant differences were observed in NIHSS or mRS at 90 days. Conclusions: Higher daily energy intake was associated with higher 90-day cognitive performance among survivors with available cognitive follow-up after mechanical thrombectomy. Given the retrospective observational design, baseline differences between exposure groups, and potential residual confounding and reverse causality, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Prospective studies are required to determine whether nutritional optimization can influence cognitive recovery after stroke.

title: AI-Guided Radiomics for Spectral-Domain OCT Characterization of Acquired Vitelliform Lesions: A Pilot Study.
abstract: Objective: To evaluate the ability of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven radiomics applied to structural OCT to characterize hypo-reflective subretinal spaces in acquired vitelliform lesions (aVLs), to distinguish reabsorbed material from subretinal fluid, improving diagnostic precision. Methods: In this retrospective monocentric study, patients with aVLs were compared with a control group of acute central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR) to provide reference OCT patterns for subretinal fluid. All participants underwent multimodal imaging. OCT scans were manually segmented. Radiomic features were extracted using a standardized pipeline, including image preprocessing, robustness assessment, variance and correlation filtering, and feature selection with a WEKA subset evaluator. A ridge-based Logistic Regression classifier was trained on 75% of the dataset and tested on the remaining 25%. Model performance was assessed using accuracy metrics, ROC AUC, and precision-recall curves. Results: A total of 520 radiomics features were extracted, of which nine were selected for training. The classifier achieved an accuracy of 86.5% in the training set (AUC 0.89; PRC 0.86) and 80% in the independent test set, with excellent AUC (0.92) and PRC (0.92). The negative predictive value reached 92%, indicating a high ability to correctly classify the aVL-associated hypo-reflective phenotype. The positive predictive value was 67%. Conclusions: AI-based radiomics demonstrated promising performance in discriminating, on structural OCT, between hypo-reflective subretinal spaces associated with the resorptive phase of aVLs and subretinal fluid. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of quantitative radiomic characterization of these two OCT phenotypes. Further studies are required to determine whether this approach may also be useful in identifying neovascular complications.

title: Predictors of Treatment Failure in the Surgical Management of Peritonsillar Abscesses.
abstract: Objectives: Peritonsillar abscess (PTA) is the most common deep neck infection and is usually managed with antibiotic therapy and surgical drainage. However, drainage may fail, leading to persistent disease, repeat intervention, tonsillectomy, or early recurrence. This study aimed to identify factors associated with drainage failure. Methods: We conducted a retrospective single-centre study of patients admitted for PTA between 2019 and 2024. All patients underwent antibiotic therapy and surgical drainage by needle aspiration or incision and drainage. Drainage failure was defined as absence of pus evacuation, lack of clinical improvement within 72 h, need for quinsy tonsillectomy (QT), or recurrence within 30 days. Clinical and radiological variables and drainage techniques were analysed using univariate and multivariable analyses. Results: Eighty-four patients were included; drainage was successful in 68 (81%) and failed in 16 (19%). Previous ipsilateral PTA, smaller abscess diameter, multiloculation, and peritonsillar abscess with a concurrent intratonsillar abscess were significantly associated with failure. Needle aspiration showed a higher failure rate than incision and drainage (33.3% vs. 12.3%; OR 3.57; 95% CI 1.16-11.00; p = 0.035), but was not significant after adjustment (OR 2.87; 95% CI 0.63-14.04; p = 0.170). Peritonsillar abscess with a concurrent intratonsillar abscess (OR 57.30; 95% CI 2.37-9371.97; p = 0.011) and previous ipsilateral PTA (OR 20.68; 95% CI 4.77-108.22; p < 0.001) were independent predictors of failure. Conclusions: Peritonsillar abscess with a concurrent intratonsillar abscess and previous ipsilateral PTA were independently associated with drainage failure. These findings may help identify patients at increased risk of unsuccessful drainage and support individualized management.

title: Ergothioneine: A Natural Antioxidant Claimed to Prevent Neurodegeneration.
abstract: Ergothioneine (ET) is an exogenous thiol antioxidant present mainly in mushrooms and, in smaller amounts, in various other food products as well. Numerous beneficial health effects of ET have been reported, suggesting that ET is a vitamin-like compound. Evidence that ET prevents and inhibits the development of neurodegenerative diseases, especially Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease, has been accumulated based on studies of cellular and animal models, as well as epidemiologic and interventional studies in humans. The mechanism of the neuroprotective action of ET remains to be elucidated. Apart from the direct antioxidant effect, ET was found to stimulate an endogenous antioxidant defense through the activation of Nrf2 signaling while also affecting other signaling pathways. The accumulating literature data suggest that an ET-rich diet could be recommended for the prevention of neurodegeneration in the general population, but such a recommendation, though noteworthy, is not yet adequately supported by the limited human intervention data, and further studies are needed.

title: An Intervention to Promote Sustainable and Inclusive Eating Behaviors in Primary and Preschools in Italy: A Pilot Study of the SoS-4-SoUPS Project.
abstract: Food waste contributes to environmental, social, economic, and nutritional losses. In this context, school canteens represent a key setting for shaping sustainable and healthy early dietary behaviors. This pilot study aimed to evaluate the implementation of a combined digital meal-planning and educational intervention and to explore changes in plate waste, food-related responses, and perceived inclusivity and involvement. An uncontrolled pre-post pilot study in one preschool and one primary school in a single municipality was conducted. The intervention combined a digital lunch-planning tool, enabling menu and portion selection, with educational workshops on food and sustainability. Plate waste was weighed during two menu-matched weeks, one before and one after implementation. Parent and child questionnaires assessing dietary habits, emotional responses to food and food waste images, perceived inclusivity and involvement, and well-being were recorded. Of 159 enrolled pupils, 155 registered on the platform and 152 used it at least once. Overall, 82.3% of meals were pre-planned through the platform. Questionnaires were completed at baseline by 93 participants and at follow-up by 60, with 48 participating at both time points. Exploratory analyses identified differences over time in some emotional-response ratings and higher parent-rated inclusivity and involvement at follow-up. Across the two observation weeks, measured plate waste decreased from 0.066 to 0.038 kg per meal attendance, an observed reduction of 42.1%. As portion sizes could be reduced or omitted, lower discarded quantities could be related to both increased food consumption and/or reduction in the amount of food prepared. High platform uptake supports the operational feasibility of implementing this combined programme in the participating schools. The observed differences are exploratory: the uncontrolled design, brief waste-measurement periods, and questionnaire attrition preclude causal attribution. Controlled studies with repeated measurements and longer follow-up are needed to evaluate effectiveness and transferability.
